page.summary: Spend a healthy state on a protection hit only when it changes a teammate's escape or rescue outcome; Mettle of Man is a conditional later payoff, not the reason to feed hits.

verdict.recommendation: Pre-position for a useful intercept, then leave once the teammate has a route. Decline hits that only create a second down.
verdict.soloQ: Commit only when the teammate's route is visible and your hit clearly buys distance; do not assume they understand a prolonged tank plan.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Call the protector, target and exit path so one health state changes the chase without pulling the whole team off objectives.
verdict.mainWeakness: Poor timing can waste a healthy state, feed a down or leave the protector exposed after a conditional perk payoff.

options.whyItsHere: After a third Protection Hit, it can shield the next attack that would down you while injured; after a full heal it reveals your aura to the Killer beyond 12/14/16 metres until deactivation on entering Dying.

opening: Before stepping into the Killer's path, verify the teammate has an escape route and you have a route after the hit.

rows.situation: A healthy protector can intercept an attack that would otherwise end a teammate's escape or rescue.
rows.action: Take one purposeful hit, then use the resulting separation to leave; do not stand for a second hit without a new payoff.
rows.why: The strategy converts a health state into teammate tempo only if the protected player gets a usable route.

rows.situation: You have earned three Protection Hits and are injured.
rows.action: Account for Mettle of Man shielding the next attack that would put you in Dying, but still plan an exit. After a full heal, account for the Killer seeing your aura at the perk's tiered long range.
rows.why: The protection is conditional, is not Endurance, and the later aura reveal is a real cost.

rows.situation: The teammate is already safe, the Killer can switch to you, or no route survives the hit.
rows.action: Stay on your current job or hand off protection to a better-positioned player.
rows.why: A hit without changed teammate outcome merely donates health and possible hook tempo.

abortWhen: Leave the protection line once the teammate has escaped it.
Do not chase a third Protection Hit when the likely result is your own down.

strengths: A correctly timed intercept can preserve a vulnerable teammate's route.
weaknesses: Consumes health and positioning; a Killer can switch targets or punish overcommitment.
commonMistakes: Taking arbitrary hits to count toward Mettle of Man.
Mistaking its shield for Endurance or ignoring the post-heal aura reveal.
